look_here_first: START WITH THE UPPER BRACTS, THEN THE ACTUAL GLAND. Native wild poinsettia, Euphorbia cyathophora, commonly has red, pink, or white patches at the BASE of green upper bracts (MODIFIED LEAVES, not petals); the bracts can sometimes be entirely green. A REAL SAVED MACRO in this lesson shows the small yellow-green CYATHIAL NECTAR GLAND with an OBLONG flattened opening and NO raised circular rim. That distinguishes it from E. heterophylla's actual photographed ROUND opening with an ANNULAR rim. Leaf shapes can be strongly variable in both plants. The larger GREEN THREE-LOBED structure is the developing CAPSULE, not the gland. Hays-target-range PASS preserved from prior verified review.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbia: milky latex; the apparent flower is a cyathium containing highly reduced male flowers and one central female flower.

key_traits.label: Growth form
key_traits.text: Annual taprooted herb; stems erect or ascending, commonly about 20–100 cm.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Usually alternate, occasionally opposite proximally; blades extremely variable—linear, lanceolate, elliptic, or broad/pandurate and sometimes lobed. Leaf shape alone is unreliable.

key_traits.label: Upper bracts
key_traits.text: Pleiochasial bracts usually green with white, pink, or red at the base; some may become wholly colored. This sharp basal color block is a strong first clue.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Usually one yellow-green gland, about 1–1.4 × 0.9–1.6 mm, sessile to substipitate; opening oblong/flattened naturally and lacking an annular rim; gland appendages absent.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Capsule green, depressed-globose to ellipsoid, about 2.8–3.2 × 4–4.5 mm, three-lobed and glabrous.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Seeds about 2.3–3.1 × 1.9–2.5 mm, rounded in cross section and tuberculate; caruncle absent.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Flowering wild poinsettia with typically sharply coral/pink/red proximal bract patches, rather than normal petals.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaves highly variable, often alternate and sometimes pandurate/lobed on the same plant.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Tiny green cyathia contain reduced flowers, not a ring of showy petals.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Glabrous, developing three-lobed green capsules; fruit shape overlaps heterophylla.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Single oblong gland opening without annular rim is decisive but unverified in current photos.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Native zone PASS already documented; do not change county audit.

key_traits.label: Reproductive teaching
key_traits.text: Cyathium = a cup-shaped Euphorbia inflorescence with highly reduced staminate flowers and one pistillate flower. The stalked swelling outside the cup becomes a THREE-LOBED capsule; upper colored or green modified leaves are BRACTS and not five separate petals. Do not mistake a ripe fruit for the nectar gland.

lookalikes.differences: Against E. heterophylla, do not rely on leaf shape. Use the bract bases and especially the cyathial gland: E. cyathophora = colored basal bracts + oblong gland opening without an annular rim; E. heterophylla = green/paler-green bracts + stipitate gland with a round opening and annular rim.
